subject: Request: custody simulation (escrow drill) + on-prem license carveouts
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Sara Bryant <sara.bryant@cortexhealth.com>, Procurement <procure@cortexhealth.com>
Cc: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-07T09:14:00Z
Subject: Request: custody simulation (escrow drill) + on-prem license carveouts

Hi Sara / Cortex team,

Following up on our private deployment conversations — Cortex is approaching final internal approvals for the on‑prem deployment, and Procurement asked us to run a simulated custody/escrow drill before signing the Order Form. The ask from your side (I understand) is to demonstrate our ability to hand over access artifacts and snapshots in a controlled, auditable way without transferring live operator credentials.

To move this forward I propose a scoped tabletop + simulated transfer as follows:
- Scope: non-production snapshot (redacted), encrypted at rest; no private key handover; handed to an agreed third‑party custodian for retrieval verification only.
- Duration: snapshot retained by custodian for up to 21 calendar days, then destroyed unless Cortex requests retention with formal approval.
- Evidence: transfer receipts, checksum, and time‑stamped retrieval log plus a short runbook describing steps.
- Contract: carve these rules into an Order Form Annex (Custody Simulation Annex) and limit operator access clauses in the MSA.

Questions for Cortex legal/procurement before we draft redlines:
1) Is 21 days an acceptable retention window for the simulation?
2) Will Cortex accept encrypted snapshots (no key handoff) as sufficient for the tabletop proof?
3) Any specific audit window or notification SLA we should mirror in the Order Form?

I've attached a proposed runbook and a short sketch of the Annex for your review (proposed-runbook-custody-drill.pdf). If you prefer, we can schedule a 30‑minute call next week to walk it through.

Thanks — aiming to keep this narrow and non-production so we don't trigger broader licensing or custody change controls.

Regards,
Mina Haddad
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0183

Attachment: proposed-runbook-custody-drill.pdf
From: Sara Bryant <sara.bryant@cortexhealth.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Cortex Health Legal <legal@cortexhealth.com>, Procurement <procure@cortexhealth.com>
Date: 2026-08-08T11:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: custody simulation (escrow drill) + on-prem license carveouts

Mina — thanks for the clear proposal and for keeping this scoped. A few notes from Procurement / Legal after an initial review:

- Retention: Procurement prefers a shorter window for the drill (10 business days) unless we see strong justification. Can you do 10 business days?
- Snapshot type: Legal says encrypted snapshot with no key handoff is acceptable, provided we get tamper-evident logs and a notarized transfer receipt from the custodian.
- Operator keys: Legal is uncomfortable with any language that could be interpreted as delegation of operator privileges. Please confirm the drill text explicitly prohibits any operational access being transferred.
- Liability / limits: Cortex Legal will want a clause that the simulation does not expand your obligations beyond what is in the MSA; they may request an explicit carve‑out in the Order Form that the drill is for verification only.

I've attached the Procurement checklist our internal GRC uses for proof-of-access exercises (ProcurementChecklist_Cortex.xlsx) — includes the minimum deliverables we expect.

If you can update your Annex sketch to reflect 10 business days, tamper logs, and an explicit no-key-handover sentence, we can route the redline to Legal for a formal pass.

Sara Bryant
Senior Manager, Cloud Procurement
Cortex Health
sara.bryant@cortexhealth.com

Attachment: ProcurementChecklist_Cortex.xlsx
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Sara Bryant <sara.bryant@cortexhealth.com>
Cc: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-09T08:27:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: custody simulation (escrow drill) + on-prem license carveouts

Sara — thanks. Appreciate the Procurement checklist; very helpful.

We can accept 10 business days retention for the simulation. To address Legal's operator key concern, we propose the following contract language snippet for an Order Form Annex (draft):

"Custody Simulation Annex — Scope and Limitations:
1. Purpose: The parties agree the purpose of the custody simulation is to verify Redwood Inference's documented snapshot packaging and transfer processes. The simulation relates only to non‑production snapshots containing customer data redacted per Cortex instructions.
2. No Operational Access: For the avoidance of doubt, the simulation shall not include transfer of live operator credentials, private keys, or any mechanism that would permit Redwood or the custodian to operate customer systems on Cortex's behalf.
3. Retention: Simulated snapshot artifacts will be retained by the custodian for a period of 10 business days and then securely deleted unless Cortex provides written instruction to retain.
4. Evidence: Redwood will provide tamper‑evident transfer logs, checksums, and a signed transfer receipt from the third‑party custodian within 48 hours of transfer completion.
5. Non‑Expansive: Participation in the simulation does not expand Redwood's technical obligations or data residency commitments beyond those stated in the MSA and Order Form.

I've attached a redline to the MSA + proposed Annex (MSA_redlines_mina_v1.docx) that inserts this Annex as an Order Form exhibit and modifies the operator access paragraph in Section 7.2 to clarify limitations.

Ben / Lauren — can Legal and Product Ops take a quick look at the redline and comment on any commercial or technical risks with the Annex wording? If we get a quick signoff from Legal we can push a clean Order Form to DocuSign next week.

Thanks,
Mina

Attachment: MSA_redlines_mina_v1.docx
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-10T15:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: custody simulation (escrow drill) + on-prem license carveouts

Looping in Legal commentary after reviewing Mina's draft Annex and the Cortex checklist. High level: good narrow approach; below are Legal's recommended edits and next steps.

1) Retention window — accept 10 business days for the drill, but add a one-time option for Cortex to request a single 10-business-day extension in writing (to handle investigations) with notification to Redwood.
2) Evidence delivery SLA — tighten to 24 hours for transfer receipts (not 48).
3) Liability carve-out — we should add an explicit sentence: "The custody simulation is solely for verification and shall not increase Redwood's liability or obligations under the MSA and shall not be a basis for any claim beyond the MSA's general warranty and limitation provisions."
4) Confidentiality / chain of custody — include a requirement that the custodian be a neutral third party with SOC 2 Type II or equivalent and sign a standard PDP (custodian data handling addendum).
5) Move: recommend placing all operational mechanics into an Order Form Annex (as you proposed) and keeping the MSA high-level to avoid changing core license scope language.

If Cortex Legal is OK with the wording above, Legal will prepare a marked-up Order Form Annex and a short email summary for signatures. I attached our commentary PDF (legal_commentary_Cortex_v01.pdf) with suggested sentence-level edits.

Action items:
- Mina: update Annex with (1) one-time extension language and (2) 24-hour evidence SLA (we can help word it).
- Alex: if commercial is comfortable with the limited extension option, confirm and I'll fold that into the clause.
- Mina / Alex: once Cortex returns a redline we should circulate a clean Order Form + Annex to Procurement / Legal and, if approved, route to DocuSign (link below).

DocuSign preview (order form): https://app.docusign.com/OrderForm/RDW-CH-0042

Ben Carter
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Attachment: legal_commentary_Cortex_v01.pdf
